highlights_headline: The upcoming 4.156 release strengthens native-platform support, fixes data and text handling, and modernizes Uno and WebAssembly integrations.
highlights_body: It raises Apple deployment baselines, moves Uno views to Uno Platform 7, and incorporates targeted m156 engine fixes. Review the migration guidance before upgrading platform-specific applications.

breaking.title: Apple platform minimums are higher
breaking.body: Native macOS now requires 11.0, while iOS, tvOS, and Mac Catalyst require 14.0. Update application deployment targets before consuming the new native assets.

breaking.title: Uno views require Uno Platform 7 and .NET 10
breaking.body: SkiaSharp.Views.Uno.WinUI now targets Uno Platform 7 and .NET 10. Upgrade Uno applications and use SKCanvasElement for GPU rendering on non-Windows Uno targets; SKSwapChainPanel uses a CPU fallback there.

breaking.title: SKData.CreateCopy validates requested array length
breaking.body: SKData.CreateCopy(byte[], ulong) now rejects a length beyond the source array with ArgumentOutOfRangeException. Pass a length within the supplied array rather than relying on an out-of-bounds native read.

breaking.title: WebGPU consumers need rebuilt WebAssembly native archives
breaking.body: WebGPU support now compiles emdawnwebgpu C++ code into libSkiaSharp.a. Rebuild custom or cached WebAssembly archives before linking .NET 8 and later WebGPU applications.

bullets.detail: Updates the bundled renderer with fixes for invalid runtime-effect types, raster-pipeline overflow handling, and BGRA uploads on GLES.

bullets.lead: Native builds use a current GN generator
bullets.detail: Updates GN for the native build while retaining SkiaSharp's established generated-header and include behavior.
Character-code APIs now decode exactly one unit for the selected text encoding, and byte-array string conversion consistently reports null arguments.

bullets.lead: Android texture rendering follows the display clock
bullets.detail: Continuous GL texture rendering is paced by Android display callbacks instead of swap throughput, while explicit rendering requests remain responsive.

bullets.lead: Managed image and text paths reduce allocations
bullets.detail: Managed pixel copies, HarfBuzz UTF-32 input, and native feature-string handling avoid unnecessary temporary allocations without changing results.

bullets.lead: Front-buffered streams retain their backing data
bullets.detail: Fixes stream ownership so front-buffered data remains available for its intended lifetime.

bullets.lead: Linux HarfBuzz keeps its bundled implementation isolated
bullets.detail: Bundled HarfBuzz function calls are bound locally on Linux, preventing conflicts with a system HarfBuzz library loaded by another component such as GTK.

bullets.lead: Uno views move to Uno Platform 7
bullets.detail: The Uno views package adopts Uno 7's unified renderer and .NET 10 baseline while preserving CPU rendering where non-Windows targets have no swap chain.

bullets.lead: Windows native components use updated platform dependencies
bullets.detail: WinUI, MAUI, Uno, and ANGLE build paths align on current Windows App SDK, WebView2, Visual Studio, and Windows SDK dependencies.
The WebGPU C++ support is included in the SkiaSharp static archive while required JavaScript glue remains a consumer link input.
